last_result.content:
## 3 De-Identification and Secondary Use

A vendor right to create de-identified data is acceptable only if all three of the following
are present. First, the de-identification standard must be objective: removal of the
identifiers enumerated in the agreement plus a determination by a qualified statistician, or
an equivalent expert-determination method, that the risk of re-identification is very small.
Stripping names and replacing an identifier with a persistent token is not sufficient.
Second, the agreement must contain an express prohibition on re-identification and on any
attempt to re-identify, binding the vendor and flowing down to its affiliates,
subprocessors, and any transferee of the data. Third, use of de-identified data must be
limited to improving the services delivered to Beacon. Sale, licensing, or other transfer of
employee-derived data to third parties, including data brokers, benchmarking consortia, and
research partners, is a rejection position and must be escalated before any concession.

last_result.content:
## 3.2 De-Identification and Analytics

Provider maintains a documented de-identification procedure under which direct identifiers,
including name, email address, employee identification number, and street address, are
removed from or replaced with a persistent pseudonymous token in a record before that record
is used for any purpose described in this Section 3.2. Provider may create De-Identified Data
from Employee Data and may use, reproduce, distribute, license, and sell De-Identified Data,
alone or combined with data from other customers, for benchmarking, research, product
development, and any other lawful business purpose, including after expiration or termination
of the Agreement. De-Identified Data is Provider's property. Customer acknowledges that
De-Identified Data is not Employee Data and that the remaining provisions of this Exhibit do
not apply to it.

action.title: Vendor Right to Re-identify De-Identified Data
action.analysis: The VitalPath Data Handling Exhibit allows VitalPath to create de-identified data using direct identifiers, but does not prohibit VitalPath from re-identifying the data or using it for purposes outside of improving the services delivered to Beacon. This is contrary to Beacon's Employee Data Protection Playbook, which requires that de-identified data cannot be re-identified and can only be used to improve services to Beacon.
action.recommendation: We should negotiate to prohibit VitalPath from re-identifying de-identified data and using it for purposes outside of improving the services delivered to Beacon.
